references.text: Describes the burnt offering ritual where blood is sprinkled on the altar and the meat is burned, consistent with the instructions in Deuteronomy regarding burnt offerings.
Explains that blood is given to make atonement on the altar, and that life is in the blood—the basis for why blood must be poured out on the Lord's altar.
Concerns the peace offering, where parts of the meat could be eaten by the one who offered it, in line with 'and you may eat the meat'.
Describes the procedure for the peace offering where blood is sprinkled around the altar, parallel to the instruction that blood must be poured on the Lord's altar.
Early instruction to offer burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar for the Lord, a fundamental parallel to the sacrificial practice described here.
Describes the consecration of the altar with burnt offerings where blood is sprinkled and the meat is burned as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
Refers to the sacrifices of the altar and points out that Jesus suffered outside the gate to sanctify the people by his own blood—the fulfillment of the meaning of blood sacrifice.
